A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe CopyrightShield and are readable throughout, including their equations, figures, and tables. V2 includes supplementary Sections 7–11; no supplement is appended to the supplied v1 PDF. The judgments concern the material actually supplied.

before.justification: V1 reports original poisoned-sample detection and defense experiments on Pokemon, including numerical results across poisoning rates and Stable Diffusion versions in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V2 reports original detection, defense, generation-quality, and ablation results on Pokemon and COYO+Midjourney, including supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: V1 detects poisoning using an IoU-gated IoU–SSCD score. V2 replaces this with normalized copyright attribution derived from spatially masked similarity and projected model gradients. The training penalty also changes from a fixed coefficient lambda to sample-specific attribution weights, substantially changing both detection and optimization.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates Pokemon character generation. V2 retains this coverage and adds a continual-pretraining scenario using COYO-700M clean images and Midjourney v5 copyright targets, extending evaluation to general imagery. SilentBadDiffusion remains the evaluated attack.

E2.justification: V1 compares defended models with undefended SilentBadDiffusion models. V2 additionally evaluates T2IShield and TERD as defense comparators in Table 2, and TRAK, Journey TRAK, and D-TRAK as detection comparators in Table 3. Previously citing some defenses did not constitute evaluating them.

E3.justification: The detection threshold sweep changes from 0.2/0.25/0.3 to 0.3/0.35/0.4, with the experimental selection changing from 0.25 to 0.35. V2 adds FID/CLIP evaluation over 500 random prompts and specifies an LDS-based threshold procedure for attribution baselines. The 100-epoch budget and 100 generated images per poisoned caption for CIR are retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds detection-only and training-only component ablations in Table 5, fixed-versus-adaptive penalty results in supplementary Table 6, and attribution-score analysis in Figure 2. V1 mentions a fixed-coefficient sweep but does not supply these comparative results. The earlier rotation and model-version analyses remain, with revised presentation.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 independent experiments per evaluated scenario without reporting seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Applying the same practice to the additional scenario does not change uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: At Pokemon poisoning rate 0.1, reported defense CIR/FAE changes from 0.318/84.13 to 0.305/85.93; the undefended values remain 0.650/50.15. These are results for the revised method and threshold, not a controlled same-procedure improvement. V2 also adds substantial baseline, COYO+Midjourney, FID/CLIP, and ablation results.

T1.justification: V2 adds projected-gradient attribution definitions and derivations, including kernel construction, Newton influence approximation, Taylor linearization, and the Johnson–Lindenstrauss lemma in Section 3.2 and supplementary Section 7. This substantially changes the mathematical development from v1's spatial-score and cross-attention motivation. The main-text and supplementary Gram-matrix expressions are not fully consistent.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds spatial-similarity detection and infringement-feature inversion for assigning responsibility. V2 drops the feature-inversion contribution and centers copyright attribution and adaptive optimization, adding a principal claim of outperforming existing defenses across two attack scenarios.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations connecting attribution scores to memorization, explaining easier detection in general imagery, and identifying detection as the stronger contributor in the component ablation. It removes v1's substantive liability-attribution discussion. The limitations concerning real-world copyrighted images and future attack methods are retained.

D1.justification: V2 adds attribution pseudocode, trigger-prompt templates, baseline implementation descriptions, and disclosures of the default SD v1.4 model, SSCD/Disc-MixUp, guidance scale 7.5, and 1000 diffusion steps. V1's explicit 832-clean-image count and 5.7-second detection timing disappear. Reproducibility remains limited by v2 specifying Adam in the main text but AdamW in the supplement.

R1.justification: V2 introduces dedicated data-attribution related work covering TRAK, Journey TRAK, and D-TRAK, and positions CopyrightShield within a detection–cleaning–retraining framework. It removes much of v1's broad adversarial-attack citation discussion and the legal-liability positioning, substantially shifting the research context.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution statements, method explanation, and substantial portions of the experimental narrative are rewritten. Related work and preliminaries are reorganized, the feature-inversion subsection is replaced by ablations, and a structured supplement is added. These changes extend beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the framework diagram, expands the rotation illustration with attribution plots, restructures tables around datasets and comparators, and replaces v1's model-version table with bar charts. It adds utility and ablation displays and supplementary comparison images, while removing the liability-allocation diagram.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical justification: evaluated competitors, component ablations, and FID/CLIP measurements address v1's missing evidence about comparative advantage, component necessity, and generation-quality costs. The additional image domain also tests broader applicability. Threshold, optimizer, and matrix-expression inconsistencies weaken reproducibility, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but these shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial improvement in experimental support.
